_comment: The eight stores, and where each page keeps its stock.
NO OPENING HOURS. Searched all eight pages for hours, opening times and
closures: there are none, because the game has none. You can shop until 2am,
which is the end of the day — the project owner confirmed this from play on
2026-08-07 and it is why `shop` is in timeNotApplicable in method_rules.json.
An empty `hours` array therefore means 'no restriction', not 'unknown', and
no shop carries an `hours` data gap.
OWNERS ARE CURATED, NOT PARSED. The infobox `residents` field lists everyone
who lives in the building — the Inn's lists six people including two children
and a travelling merchant. The page prose says who runs the place, and three
shops are run by more than one person, so `owner` is the single clear
proprietor and `staff` is everyone the page names. Nora and Holt run the
General Store jointly; neither is 'the' owner, so it has staff and no owner.
STOCK SECTIONS ARE DECLARED. Every page arranges its headings differently:
'Stock', '=Stock=', 'Year-Round Stock', 'Farm Supplies'. Worse, Hayden's page
has tables for selling animals back and for daycare pricing, which are not
stock at all and would otherwise be read as things you can buy. Rules match a
case-insensitive substring of the heading path; `ignoreSections` records the
tables we are deliberately skipping and why. A table under any other heading
produces a warning, so a new stock section surfaces instead of vanishing.
SEASONS. Only the General Store's seed tables are season-gated, and the page
says so in the heading. Everything else is year-round — including Balor's,
whose page states outright that stock is not restricted by season.
SATURDAY MARKET IS NOT HERE. Its eight vendors live on an event page with a
different structure, and their stock is day-of-week gated. That is a separate
piece of work rather than something to half-do here.
_priceTokens: `{{Price|N|token}}` is used for far more than money. The same template
prices a cost, a defence stat and a required cooking level, so a row can
carry three of them and picking the first put '2 defense' in the price
`priceTokens` maps the tokens that ARE currencies. `nonPriceTokens` names
the ones that are deliberately not, so an unrecognised token is a build
warning rather than a silent default to tesserae — which would invent a

nonPriceTokens.reason: an armour stat, in the Defense column
the Cooking level a recipe needs, not a cost
an animal's heart level, on Hayden's tables

ignoreSections.reason: forging recipes, which belong to recipes and are gated on Blacksmithing rather than bought
house upgrades, which land with buildings
land expansion, which lands with buildings
a service price, not an item you can buy
what Hayden pays YOU, the opposite of stock
